source.title: Toward a Theory of Generalizability in LLM Mechanistic Interpretability Research

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but its own experiment measures attention-head behavior and developmental trajectories, not representational distances or any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The empirical results concern 1-back attention-head behavior across Pythia seeds and sizes. They do not measure representation alignment as defined in the claim. Rows below record the related mechanistic-convergence findings under versions ["none"]. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study measures how strongly Pythia attention heads attend to the previous token (1-back attention) across checkpoints, seeds and sizes. It also correlates these developmental trajectories between model instances. It never compares representations, never maps one model's representations onto another's, and never identifies shared features or subspaces. Its cross-size finding is that trajectory correlation is higher for larger models. The author calls this possibly consistent with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but it concerns when an attention behaviour emerges, not representational alignment. Heads' function was not established: the author says attention behaviour is necessary but not sufficient. So the recurrence of 1-back heads does not amount to a test of universal features or circuits (V5). Across seeds, 1-back attention appears consistently but in variable layers. This loosely echoes V3's 'same features, different units', but the measure is a max-over-heads attention score, not feature or subspace identity. All models share architecture family and training data.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author finds strong developmental (temporal) correspondence of putative 1-back attention across Pythia seeds and sizes but limited positional correspondence. Larger models show earlier onset, steeper slope and higher peak. Cross-architecture temporal convergence is higher for larger pairs, which the author calls 'possibly consistent' with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. The paper's main contribution is a conceptual framework of axes of correspondence for generalizing mechanistic claims.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures attention-head trajectories and their correlations, rather than comparing representations or using the original source's representational-similarity method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that developmental results were qualitatively similar under an alternative 1-back-attention operationalization and across Natural Stories; it notes that positional results were not qualitatively identical under the alternative operationalization.

fits_no_version.finding: 1-back attention trajectories correlate very highly across seeds of the same architecture (M=0.99) and across architectures (M=0.95).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Developmental timing of simple attention behaviours converges across seeds and sizes of models trained on the same data.

fits_no_version.finding: Among different-size pairs, trajectory correlation rises with each model's parameter count (β=0.03). MDS separation ratios fall from 14M (11.4) to 160M (2.42), but 410M is 4.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal convergence of attention-head development increases with model size, non-monotonically (a developmental analogue of scale convergence).

fits_no_version.finding: Larger models show earlier onset (β=−0.18), steeper slope (β=0.01) and higher peak (β=0.07) of 1-back attention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Developmental profile of a given attention behaviour varies systematically with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer position of 1-back heads varies across seeds and models (e.g., layer 3 or 4 in 14M). Later layers show less 1-back attention (β=−0.11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention mechanisms recur across seeds in consistent timing but not consistent location.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The empirical reference class is limited to random seeds and sizes of Pythia models trained on the same data. The paper states that attention behavior is a necessary but insufficient prerequisite for establishing the heads' function; the functional role was not investigated. Positional consistency was limited, and some reported trajectory details are presented only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Individual seed/head trajectories and plotted point-level values in Figures 1, 2, 4, and 6 were not extracted because the text does not provide their individual numeric values; the textually described aggregates and statistics are included.

untested.parts: Representational similarity between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives or data, and its change with scale.
Shared features or subspaces across seeds; only an attention-pattern statistic and its position were tracked.
Any mapping, stitching or relative-representation transfer between models.
Recurrence of functionally identified features or circuits; 1-back heads were defined by attention behaviour only, without functional validation.
Dependence of representational similarity on metric or inputs. The input-robustness check (Appendix B) concerns attention trajectories only.
Plateau or causes of representational alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's rows and gate are accurate. No row bears on a claim version, because attention-behaviour trajectories are a different construct from representational alignment. The PRH link is the author's speculative interpretation, not a test. The reference class is narrow: Pythia seeds and sizes, same data, 14M–410M.

versions.untested_parts: Representational similarity between independently trained models and whether it rises with model size and capability.
Cross-modal vision-language alignment on paired images and captions, and its relationship to model quality.
Whether seeds learn the same features or shared subspaces; the study tracks attention behavior, not feature or subspace identity.
Mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment between model representations.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of representational convergence on similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions.
Whether representational alignment plateaus or is explained by shared data or objectives.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M, Pythia-70M, Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M (all models and seeds)
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximum 1-back attention across training checkpoints and fit a generalized additive model to the pooled trajectories.
rows.measure: Fit of GAM predicting maximum 1-back attention from log training step; reported developmental timing.
rows.value: R2 = 0.95; expected onset between 512 and 2000 steps; selective 1-back attention tended to emerge around 10^3 training steps, corresponding to roughly 2B tokens.
rows.note: Pooled result across models and seeds. It concerns developmental correspondence in an attention pattern, not representational distance.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M, Pythia-70M, Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Regressed each seed's 1-back attention onset measure against log parameter count, with seed as a random intercept.

conditions.value: range 0.01 to 0.3, averaged across threshold results

rows.measure: Association between log parameter count and onset measure.
rows.note: The text reports larger models had an earlier onset of 1-back attention; this is not a representational-alignment measure.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M, Pythia-70M, Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Regressed each seed's 1-back attention trajectory slope against log parameter count, with seed as a random intercept.

conditions.value: slope of maximum 1-back attention against log training step

rows.measure: Association between log parameter count and trajectory slope.
rows.note: The text reports steeper attention-growth slopes for larger models.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M, Pythia-70M, Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Regressed each seed's maximum 1-back attention peak against log parameter count, with seed as a random intercept.
rows.measure: Association between log parameter count and peak attention.
rows.note: The text reports higher attention peaks for larger models.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M, Pythia-70M, Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Compared attention to the immediately preceding token across layers and seeds.
rows.measure: Positional consistency of putative 1-back heads; mixed-effects association between layer depth and average 1-back attention.
rows.value: Positional consistency was described as relatively low and more variable across seeds and especially models; some evidence showed a middle-layer peak. Layer Depth β = −0.11.
rows.note: The study describes positional consistency as limited; individual layer-wise values are shown in figures.

rows.operation_detail: Calculated Pearson correlations between pairs of 1-back attention trajectories.
rows.note: Aggregate mean across same-architecture seed pairs.

rows.subject: Pythia seeds from different architectures
rows.operation_detail: Calculated Pearson correlations between pairs of 1-back attention trajectories.

rows.subject: Pythia seeds from same and different architectures
rows.operation_detail: Regressed pairwise trajectory correlation on whether the pair was the same model and on each model's parameter count.

conditions.value: same-model indicator and parameter counts of both models

rows.value: Same Model β = 0.05; each Number of Parameters predictor β = 0.03.
rows.uncertainty: Same Model: SE = 0.002, p < .001; Number of Parameters: SE = 0.002, p < .001
rows.note: The paper reports higher temporal correlations for same-architecture seeds and for larger models, holding the same-model predictor constant.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M seeds
rows.operation_detail: Compared maximum 1-back attention trajectories across stories in the Natural Stories Corpus.

conditions.value: each story in the Natural Stories Corpus

rows.measure: Consistency of developmental trajectories across input stories.
rows.value: Trajectories were described as extremely similar, with attention changes beginning around 10^3 training steps across all seeds and stories.
rows.note: This input-sensitivity check concerns attention trajectories, not representational convergence.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M, Pythia-70M, Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Applied multidimensional scaling to the correlation matrix of model-instance trajectory pairs and calculated separation ratios by model class.

conditions.value: separation ratio of seed clusters based on trajectory correlations

rows.note: The text says the ratio declines with size through 160M, while 410M is higher than 70M and 160M but lower than 14M; it interprets larger different-architecture models as relatively more similar along the temporal axis.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
